name: economics
tier_note: Tiers = REASONING difficulty (T1 = a named figure + one seen/unseen moment or incentive a kid can spot .. T5 = the deep Austrian argument with the full seen/unseen/knowledge-problem chain and its historical vindication or refutation), NOT obscurity. Grade-10 HARD ceiling: no college-level monetary math (Phillips curves, IS-LM, DSGE, Cobb-Douglas, Lagrangians, Bellman equations, marginal rate of substitution as jargon) -- Austrian technical vocabulary appears ONLY tied to the reasoning move it names (Cantillon effect OK as 'proximity to money issuance', calculation debate OK as 'central planners cannot know what dispersed prices signal'). Aim ~30%+ of rungs at T1-T2 (every named figure -- Mises, Hayek, Bastiat, Rothbard, Sowell, Buchanan, Friedman -- gets a T1/T2 foundational anchor before being referenced at T3+; per SHARED_PRINCIPLES teach-before-test). Operative gameplay gate = TOTAL record chars (stem + 4 choices): T1<=460, T2<=680, T3<=850, T4<=1000, T5<=1150; context is UNCAPPED (read only AFTER the answer, off the timer). Economics is THRESHOLD mode (lockpicking), ~65s timer at WIS 10 (SUBJECT_TIMER 48 + 1.7/WIS -- most generous in the game by design; economics stems carry dense reasoning-chain scaffolding); no same-FACT repeats within a ladder (same-TOPIC deepening is the goal; each rung a DIFFERENT reasoning move or historical case).
voice_rule:
ECONOMICS = the BASTIAT PATTERN, REASONING-LED: the most memorable economics question reveals a HIDDEN COST, INCENTIVE, KNOWLEDGE-PROBLEM, or CYCLE. This bank teaches a kid to see the unseen -- to spot what a policy costs beyond its stated benefit, to see what incentives it creates, to grasp what no central planner can know, and to recognize the boom-bust cycle as a monetary phenomenon.
  ANSWER HIERARCHY (Bastiat Pattern):
  (1) SEEN-VS-UNSEEN RECOGNITION (highest) -- kid spots the hidden cost or unseen consequence (broken-window: the money spent on the glazier CANNOT be spent on the tailor -- the tailor's lost sale is UNSEEN; minimum wage: the worker whose job is priced out of existence is UNSEEN; tariffs: the consumer paying more for domestic goods is UNSEEN).
  (2) INCENTIVE RECOGNITION -- public choice (Buchanan + Tullock), regulatory capture (Stigler 1971), rent-seeking (Tullock 1967), moral hazard (bailouts create MORE risk-taking, not less), dispersed costs + concentrated benefits (Olson 1965 -- why farm subsidies survive despite most citizens paying).
  (3) KNOWLEDGE-PROBLEM RECOGNITION (Hayek) -- what no central planner has (Mises 1920 calculation debate: without market prices no rational allocation; Hayek 1945 'The Use of Knowledge in Society' -- the dispersed knowledge in millions of heads is IRREDUCIBLE to any central agency).
  (4) CYCLE RECOGNITION -- ABCT (Austrian Business Cycle Theory: artificially low interest rates cause malinvestment -> boom -> inevitable bust), fiat-dies-historically (every fiat currency in history has been debased or collapsed -- Diocletian's denarius, Weimar mark, Zimbabwe dollar, Argentine peso), boom-bust as MONETARY phenomenon not psychological (Mises + Hayek + Rothbard vs Keynes's 'animal spirits').
  (5) GENERIC LABELS -- BANNED as primary answers ('capitalism', 'socialism', 'the free market', 'the government', 'inflation', 'the economy'). A rung whose answer is 'inflation' is DEAD -- rewrite so the answer is the Cantillon effect, or the specific monetary event (1971 Nixon shock closes the gold window), or the named policy (QE, ZIRP), or the named economist's insight ('Milton Friedman: inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon').
  THE DINNER TEST: does the ANSWER ALONE make a parent ask 'wait, what?' If 'capitalism' stops conversation cold but 'Frederic Bastiat's petition of the candlemakers demanding a law against the sun' makes them ask WHO, you wrote the wrong question.
  RECOGNITION-NOT-VERDICT TEST (feedback-surface-good-critique): on policy questions, the answer names the CRITIC'S REASONING MOVE, never the policy verdict. WRONG: 'What is wrong with minimum wage?' -> 'It causes unemployment.' RIGHT: 'A senator proposes doubling the minimum wage to help low-wage workers. Which classical critique does Milton Friedman press?' -> 'That the worker priced out of the labor market is UNSEEN; judge by results not intentions.' The student walks the chain themselves.
  TWO ladder SHAPES:
  (A) FIGURE/CONCEPT/EVENT ladder -- ONE Austrian figure, one core concept, or one historical event deepened across tiers: Frederic Bastiat (T1 who was he -> T2 the broken window story -> T3 the petition of the candlemakers -> T4 the negative railway argument -> T5 'That Which is Seen and That Which is Not Seen' as the founding method of economic reasoning); the 1971 Nixon shock (T1 what did Nixon do -> T2 the gold window closed -> T3 Bretton Woods dies -> T4 how oil-shock inflation followed -> T5 why every fiat since has been a pure political-promise currency).
  (B) CONCEPT/PATTERN ladder -- ONE reasoning move deepened ACROSS cases: seen-vs-unseen applied to broken windows / minimum wage / tariffs / stimulus / Cash for Clunkers; the knowledge problem applied to price controls / rent control / central bank rate-setting / socialist calculation; moral hazard applied to bank bailouts / FDIC / too-big-to-fail / student loans. Pattern ladders carry the analytic backbone (~25%+) and native T4/T5 ceiling.
  SCENE-LED, NEVER DEFINITION-SHELL: HARD BANS on cold stems -- 'What is Y?' / 'Define X.' / 'What is the Austrian school?' / bare-jargon-recall. ALWAYS a scene then a pointed question: a policy proposal, a historical moment, a named argument, a specific chart-point.
  ONE COHERENT REASONING MOVE PER RUNG: setup + answer are the SAME logical beat; two arguments = two rungs; no decoration-mismatch (an interesting-but-unrelated case study stapled in front of a different reasoning move is BANNED); no move-stacking.
  REASONING-IN-STEM-NOT-CONTEXT: the substantive setup lives in the STEM (the policy proposal, the historical moment, the price chart); context (after the answer, off the timer) may deepen it but never carry the reasoning move.
  DISTRACTOR & ANTI-RESTATEMENT DISCIPLINE (REASONING subject -- a careful kid reasoning to the answer IS the skill, NOT a telegraph): stem sets up the SCENE and the OPPOSING position, never the CRITIC'S move; if the stem describes the reasoning-move and the answer merely names it, that is RESTATEMENT. ALL FOUR choices stay LIVE given everything the stem says. DISTRACTORS ARE OTHER REAL REASONING MOVES applied to other scenarios: seen-vs-unseen / knowledge-problem / moral-hazard / dispersed-costs / public-choice / regulatory-capture / 'compared to what?' / 'judge by results not intentions' -- used HONESTLY. Never joke options. CHOICE PARITY: all four structurally parallel (answer a reasoning move -> all four reasoning moves; answer a named figure -> all four named figures; no lone-long, lone-number standout).
  SHARED_PRINCIPLES story-in-stem, no-weasel-closers ('Which move does the critic press?' not 'What is the takeaway?'), teach-before-test (every major named figure -- Bastiat, Mises, Hayek, Rothbard, Friedman, Sowell, Buchanan, Satoshi, Hal Finney -- needs a T1 or T2 foundational anchor before being referenced at T3+).
  ACCURACY RAILS (non-negotiable -- this is for real children): every name, argument, quote, dataset, and historical event REAL and correctly attributed; NO fabricated statistics; specific dates and figures verified (Nixon shock August 15 1971; Jekyll Island November 1910; Mises's Economic Calculation in the Socialist Commonwealth 1920; Hayek's Use of Knowledge 1945; Satoshi's white paper October 31 2008; the Bitcoin genesis block January 3 2009 embedding the Times headline 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks'); NO confusing Austrian figures (Rothbard was not Mises; Salerno is not Hoppe); the communism death toll of 65-100M is Black Book of Communism (Courtois 1997) -- cite that source when the number appears.
  LANE BORDERS (seven shipped sisters share this world -- respect the borders): HISTORY covers actual wars, empires, treaties, kings-as-heads-of-state; economics covers the ECONOMIC REASONING behind or about historical events (Great Depression as monetary failure per Friedman + Schwartz = economics; the Wall Street Crash timeline = history). GEOGRAPHY covers places; economics covers the economic conditions AT places (Venezuela's oil-and-price-controls collapse as economic case = economics; Venezuela as country = geography). PHILOSOPHY covers moral reasoning generally; economics covers ECONOMIC reasoning specifically (Rawls's veil of ignorance = philosophy; Buchanan's constitutional political economy = economics -- both use veil-shaped arguments but the specific institutional analysis is economics). SCIENCE covers empirical methodology; economics is a REASONING subject and the answer is a reasoning MOVE, not a controlled experiment (Austrian critique of positivist economics -- 'human action is not laboratory chemistry' -- is itself a legitimate economics topic).
  OUT entirely: college-level monetary math (see tier_note); pure political-history without an economic-reasoning payoff; comparative-religion or comparative-mythology economic claims; MMT / Keynesian doctrine presented uncritically (they appear only PRESENTED + REFUTED, per stance); ESG / DEI / sustainability finance as neutral-fact (they appear only as regulatory-capture case studies); no fabricated Austrian legends or unsourced quotes; no confusing Bitcoin with 'crypto' generally.
framing:
The economics bank teaches a kid to reason like a Bastiat + Hayekian: to SEE THE UNSEEN, to spot the incentive, to grasp the knowledge problem, to recognize monetary cycles. Brandon holds Austrian-libertarian + Bitcoin-maximalist convictions and the bank reflects those seriously -- NOT as tribal identity, but as the intellectually defensible positions that the historical record VINDICATES (Mises 1920 predicting socialist calculation failure vindicated by USSR collapse; Hayek 1945 predicting price-signal irreducibility vindicated by every planned-economy shortage; ABCT predicting boom-bust from artificially low rates vindicated by 2008 GFC; Bitcoin as sound-money engineering vindicated by 2020-24 fiat-debasement + adoption cycle).
  RECOGNITION-NOT-VERDICT (feedback-surface-good-critique -- the load-bearing pedagogical rule): on policy questions, teach the kid to RECOGNIZE the reasoning move, NEVER to memorize the verdict. Question shape: an advocate proposes a policy -> a named critic articulates a specific reasoning move -> the answer names the CRITIC'S move (Bastiat / Hayek / Buchanan / Sowell / Friedman / Olson / Stigler / Tullock). Choices are other real critical moves. The bank NEVER closes with 'the policy is bad' or 'the critic is correct' -- it closes with 'the critic's reasoning move is X.' Kid walks the chain themselves.
  PILLAR SHARES (~350 topics total, ~2,500-3,000 Q, matching the wonder-bank scale of geography/science/theology):
  P1 AUSTRIAN FOUNDATIONS ~17% (~60 topics) -- Menger (subjective value, marginal analysis, 1871 Principles of Economics); Bohm-Bawerk (capital theory, roundabout production, Marx-refutation); Mises (Human Action, praxeology, 1920 calculation debate, ABCT as monetary theory, methodological individualism); Hayek (Use of Knowledge 1945, Road to Serfdom, spontaneous order, the 1974 Nobel, the pretense of knowledge Nobel lecture); Rothbard (Man Economy and State, America's Great Depression, For a New Liberty, ethics of liberty); Kirzner (entrepreneurship as alertness to disequilibrium); Salerno + Boettke + Hoppe as modern Austrian continuators. Every rung teaches a REASONING MOVE, not a biographical trivia.
  P2 BASTIAT + SEEN/UNSEEN TRADITION ~14% (~50 topics) -- Bastiat's 1850 'That Which is Seen and That Which is Not Seen' as the founding method; the broken-window fallacy (the shopkeeper's son breaks a pane -- the glazier's job is SEEN, the tailor's foregone sale is UNSEEN); the negative railway argument (why not break every rail line to create more jobs at every stop?); the petition of the candlemakers (satirical demand for a law against the sun to protect domestic light-makers -- prefiguring modern protectionism); The Law (1850) on the perversion of legal force. Applied to modern policies: minimum wage (unseen: the worker priced out), tariffs (unseen: the consumer paying more), Cash for Clunkers (unseen: the used-car market destroyed), stimulus (unseen: the private investment crowded out), rent control (unseen: the housing stock depleted).
  P3 SOUND MONEY + BITCOIN ~20% (~70 topics -- the flagship pillar) -- Gold standard history (Bretton Woods 1944, Nixon shock August 15 1971, the last day of any real gold-money link); fiat-currency-dies-historically (Diocletian's denarius debasement, Weimar 1923 hyperinflation, Zimbabwe 2008 100-trillion-dollar note, Venezuela 2018-, Argentine peso cycles); Cantillon effect (proximity to money-issuance -> asymmetric benefit); BITCOIN in depth: Satoshi Nakamoto (the white paper October 31 2008, the genesis block January 3 2009 embedding the Times headline, Satoshi's disappearance in April 2011, his last known email to Mike Hearn); Hal Finney (running the first node, Cypherpunk history, receiving the first Bitcoin transaction, his ALS letter 'Bitcoin's founder', posthumous cryonics); cypherpunk lineage (David Chaum's DigiCash, Adam Back's Hashcash, Wei Dai's b-money, Nick Szabo's bit gold); mining mechanics (proof-of-work, halving cycles every 4 years, difficulty adjustment, ASIC evolution, mining pool dynamics); custody (self-custody vs exchange custody, 'not your keys not your coins', Mt Gox 2014 collapse, FTX 2022 collapse); the 21 million cap; lightning network; adoption milestones (Silk Road 2011-13, first Bitcoin pizza May 22 2010 -- 10K BTC for two pizzas, MicroStrategy accumulation 2020-, El Salvador legal tender 2021, spot ETFs January 2024). Altcoins appear as CAUTIONARY FOILS not primary content (Ethereum's move from PoW to PoS -- was it a security all along?; the endless Layer-1 airdrop grift cycle; the 2017 ICO bubble; NFT bubble 2021-22).
  P4 FEDERAL RESERVE + CENTRAL BANKING CAPTURE ~14% (~50 topics) -- The Fed's founding (Jekyll Island November 1910 secret meeting -- Warburg, Aldrich, Rockefeller-Morgan interests; the Federal Reserve Act 1913); the Great Depression as MONETARY FAILURE (Friedman + Schwartz A Monetary History of the United States 1963 showing the Fed contracted the money supply 33% 1929-33); Bretton Woods breakdown (Nixon shock 1971); Volcker's inflation-crushing 1979-82 (Fed funds rate 20%, back-to-back recessions, dollar restored); Greenspan-Bernanke era (Greenspan Put, 2001 rate cuts driving housing bubble, Bernanke QE 2008 onward); ZIRP era (2008-15 zero rates + QE1/QE2/QE3, asset price inflation, Cantillon-effect winners); COVID monetary response 2020-21 ($3T balance-sheet expansion in weeks, the resulting 2021-23 inflation, the Fed's 'transitory' error, Powell's aggressive 2022-23 tightening); modern critics (Ron Paul Audit the Fed, Wright Patman-tradition congressional critics, Austrian economists on Fed's failures).
  P5 COMMUNISM + PLANNING FAILURE ~14% (~50 topics) -- The socialist calculation debate (Mises 1920, Lange-Lerner response 1930s, Hayek 1935 Collectivist Economic Planning, the debate the Austrians CLEARLY won by 1989); Holodomor 1932-33 (Ukrainian famine, 3.5-7.5M deaths, Stalin's grain requisitions, Duranty's New York Times cover-up, the term 'kulak' used to dehumanize); Great Leap Forward 1958-62 (Mao's collectivization, backyard steel furnaces, 15-45M deaths -- highest human-caused death toll in history); Khmer Rouge 1975-79 (Year Zero, Killing Fields, 1.5-2M deaths of ~7-8M population); Gulag system (~1.5-1.7M documented deaths, 18M through the system, Solzhenitsyn); Venezuela 2013- (price controls, Maduro, hyperinflation, mass emigration -- the ONLY modern case study of socialism-in-real-time for a Western student); East Germany Stasi + Berlin Wall (137 shot trying to escape, the calculation debate made physical); the Black Book of Communism 1997 documenting 65-100M total deaths across regimes; price-control failures throughout history (Diocletian's Edict on Maximum Prices 301 AD; Nixon 1971 wage/price freeze; 1970s gas lines from price caps; modern rent control cities).
  P6 PUBLIC CHOICE + REASONING-MOVE RECOGNITION ~21% (~75 topics) -- Buchanan + Tullock The Calculus of Consent 1962 (public choice theory: politicians are self-interested actors, not benevolent planners); Buchanan's 1986 Nobel Prize; Stigler 1971 The Theory of Economic Regulation (regulators get captured by the industries they regulate -- documented in FCC, ICC, CAB); Olson 1965 The Logic of Collective Action (dispersed costs + concentrated benefits -> concentrated beneficiaries organize, dispersed victims don't -- why farm subsidies survive); Tullock's rent-seeking (deadweight loss from lobbying for privileges); moral hazard (bank bailouts create MORE risk-taking not less; too-big-to-fail 2008 institutionalized it); Coase 1960 The Problem of Social Cost (transaction costs, not externalities-as-such); Sowell's 'compared to what?' (any policy critique must name the counterfactual -- 'imperfect market' vs WHAT imperfect government); Friedman's 'judge by results, not intentions' (the road to hell is paved with them). Reasoning-move recognition ladders where an advocate proposes a policy and a named critic identifies the specific move (this is the LARGEST pillar because it's where the pedagogical yield is highest -- kid learns the moves, not the verdicts).
  STANCE (SUPREME per moral_vision.md sec 6 + 9 + feedback-economics-voice + feedback-surface-good-critique):
  AUSTRIAN SCHOOL = CORRECT: Menger's subjective value, Mises's calculation problem, Hayek's knowledge problem, ABCT VINDICATED by the historical record (1929-33 as Fed error, 1970s stagflation, 2008 GFC predicted by Austrian analysts, 2020-24 post-COVID inflation as ABCT-predicted monetary phenomenon).
  FED = CRITICAL CONCERN: 1913 Jekyll Island founding, 1929-33 error (per Friedman + Schwartz -- even Milton Friedman said the Fed caused the Great Depression by contracting money supply 33%), 1971 Nixon shock closing the gold window, 2008 GFC + Bernanke QE, 2020-24 inflation as monetary failure. Not 'the Fed is evil'; the Fed is INSTITUTIONALLY CAPTURED and consistently WRONG about the biggest calls.
  COMMUNISM = 65-100M deaths, FACT (Black Book of Communism 1997). Not contested. Not 'both sides tried their best.' The calculation debate was WON by 1989.

MMT: 2021-23 inflation falsified Kelton's central claim that the constraint on money-printing is real resources not political will.
  BITCOIN = GREAT HUMAN ACHIEVEMENT. Not 'crypto' generally. Bitcoin specifically: sound money engineering, proof-of-work security, 21M cap, self-custody sovereignty, the answer to the political-money problem the Austrians identified. Cypherpunk lineage celebrated.
  PUBLIC CHOICE + SPONTANEOUS ORDER = CELEBRATED: Buchanan + Tullock, Hayek, all vindicated. Government failure is a REAL failure mode, not a slur.

The mainstream economics profession's failure to predict 2008 + 2020-24 inflation is the institutional-capture pattern this bank teaches kids to recognize.
  RECOGNITION-NOT-VERDICT (the pedagogical rail): on policy topics the answer names the CRITIC'S REASONING MOVE. The critic's conclusion is separate; the student can accept or reject it. The bank teaches the MOVE, not the verdict.
